lem:gap-mass-summability.label: Lemma 6.50 (Summability of one gap length per level)

They also record that <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>n</mi></msub><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>n</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_n g_n</annotation></semantics></math> converges and that its tails tend to <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mn>0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math>.

lem:half-divisor-unit-drop.label: Lemma 6.51 (The effect of adding one divisor)
lem:half-divisor-unit-drop.note: The Lean identity <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>∪</mo><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">{</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">}</mo></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>A</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">)</mo><mo>+</mo><msub><mn mathvariant="bold">𝟏</mn><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>∣</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{A\cup\{d\}}(m)=c_A(m)+\mathbf 1_{d\mid m}</annotation></semantics></math> holds for every positive <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math>, every set <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>⊆</mo><mi mathvariant="double-struck">ℕ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A\subseteq\mathbb N</annotation></semantics></math>, finite or infinite, and every <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>∉</mo><mi>A</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d\notin A</annotation></semantics></math>; the printed statement is its case of a finite support <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_0</annotation></semantics></math> and <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>N</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d=N+1</annotation></semantics></math>. The value <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math> at <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m=2(N+1)</annotation></semantics></math> is also stated separately for finite binary words.

lem:half-endpoint-kills.label: Lemma 6.38 (No finite Mersenne sum equals one half)
lem:half-endpoint-kills.note: The Lean statements have the same conclusions as the printed ones; the second holds for every finite <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mi>u</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u</annotation></semantics></math> and every <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d\ge0</annotation></semantics></math>, where an index <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mn>0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math> in <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mi>u</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u</annotation></semantics></math> contributes nothing to <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X_u(2)</annotation></semantics></math>. Their proofs use the printed reasons: the reduced denominator of <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X_u(2)</annotation></semantics></math> is odd, and the full Mersenne sum is irrational.

lem:largest-false-rank-algebra.label: Lemma 6.42 (The exact gap at the largest omitted rank)

decls.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR21.largest_false_rank_algebra
decls.sig:
theorem largest_false_rank_algebra {s d : ℕ} {u : Finset ℕ}
    (hd2 : 2 ≤ d) (hds : d < s) (hu : ∀ e ∈ u, 2 ≤ e ∧ e < d)
    (hlate : 2 * s < 3 * d) :
    3 * rowWeightSum s (u ∪ Finset.Ico (d + 1) s)
        + (3 * 2 ^ (s + 1) + 2 * 4 ^ (s - d) + 4)
      = 3 * rowWeightSum s (insert d u)

decls.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR21.paper_largest_false_rank_algebra
decls.sig:
theorem paper_largest_false_rank_algebra :
    (∀ (s d : ℕ) (u : Finset ℕ), 2 ≤ d → d < s → (∀ e ∈ u, 2 ≤ e ∧ e < d) →
        2 * s < 3 * d →
        3 * rowWeightSum s (u ∪ Finset.Ico (d + 1) s)
            + (3 * 2 ^ (s + 1) + 2 * 4 ^ (s - d) + 4)
          = 3 * rowWeightSum s (insert d u)) ∧
    (∀ (s d : ℕ) (hs : 5 ≤ s), IsLargestFalseRank (seamGreedyWord s) d →
        ¬ SeamGreedyUpperOrMiddleAt s hs →
        IsLargestFalseRank (seamGreedyWord (s + 1)) d) ∧
    (∀ (s : ℕ) (hs : 5 ≤ s), SeamGreedyUpperOrMiddleAt s hs →
        IsLargestFalseRank (seamGreedyWord (s + 1)) s)

lem:linear-channel-nogo.label: Lemma 6.47 (Linear functionals factoring through one value)
lem:linear-channel-nogo.note: The Lean factorisation <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">v</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">)</mo><mspace width="0.167em"></mspace><msub><mi>w</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Lambda(v)=\mathrm{ev}(v)\,w_0</annotation></semantics></math> holds for a linear map <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Lambda</annotation></semantics></math> into any <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mi mathvariant="double-struck">ℚ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb Q</annotation></semantics></math>-vector space <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mi>W</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W</annotation></semantics></math> whose kernel contains <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ker</mi><mo>⁡</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">v</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ker(\mathrm{ev})</annotation></semantics></math>; the printed identity is its case <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>W</mi><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="double-struck">ℚ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W=\mathbb Q</annotation></semantics></math>, <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>ℓ</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Lambda=\ell_j</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>ℓ</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">(</mo><mi>e</mi><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_0=\ell_j(e)</annotation></semantics></math>. The vanishing of every square minor of order at least two is the second Lean statement (a square matrix <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>ℓ</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">)</mo><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\ell_j(v_i))</annotation></semantics></math> over an index set with at least two elements), and rank at most one follows from the <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>×</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\times2</annotation></semantics></math> minors.

lem:mersenne-tail-weight.label: Lemma 6.34 (Each Mersenne weight exceeds its remaining tail)
lem:mersenne-tail-weight.note: The Lean lower bound is <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi>−</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mstyle displaystyle="false"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mstyle><mspace width="0.167em"></mspace><msup><mn>4</mn><mrow><mi>−</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></msup><mo><</mo><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>n</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2^{-n}+\tfrac13\,4^{-n}<R_n</annotation></semantics></math>, sharper than the printed <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi>−</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></msup><mo><</mo><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>n</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2^{-n}<R_n</annotation></semantics></math>, and this bound, the identity <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>R</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_n=w_{n+1}+R_{n+1}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo>≤</mo><mn>2</mn><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_n\le2w_{n+1}</annotation></semantics></math> hold for every <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n\ge0</annotation></semantics></math>; the printed statement takes <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n\ge1</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo><</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>n</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2w_{n+1}<w_n</annotation></semantics></math> and <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo><</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>n</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_n<w_n</annotation></semantics></math> are as printed. The remark on the totient weights is the arithmetic <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>φ</mi><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">)</mo><mi>/</mi><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>φ</mi><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">)</mo><mi>/</mi><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>5</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mi>φ</mi><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">)</mo><mi>/</mi><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varphi(4)/2^4+\varphi(5)/2^5=\frac14=\varphi(3)/2^3</annotation></semantics></math>, outside the Lean statements.

lem:mixed-prime-power-layer.label: Lemma 6.57 (Commuting prime-power differences)
lem:mixed-prime-power-layer.note: The Lean statements have the same hypotheses and conclusions as the printed ones, with the commutation proved for every <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>e</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p,e</annotation></semantics></math> and every <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> defined on all of <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mi mathvariant="double-struck">ℕ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb N</annotation></semantics></math>. The right side of the mixed identity is written as <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><msup><mi>A</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></msub><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{A'}(n)</annotation></semantics></math> with <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>A</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">{</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>:</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">gcd</mi><mo>⁡</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>p</mi><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mspace width="0.222em"></mspace><msup><mi>p</mi><mi>e</mi></msup><msup><mi>q</mi><mi>f</mi></msup><mi>d</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A'=\{d:\gcd(d,pq)=1,\ p^eq^fd\in A\}</annotation></semantics></math>, which equals <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>∣</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><msub><mn mathvariant="bold">𝟏</mn><mi>A</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">(</mo><msup><mi>p</mi><mi>e</mi></msup><msup><mi>q</mi><mi>f</mi></msup><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{d\mid n}\mathbf 1_A(p^eq^fd)</annotation></semantics></math> because every divisor of <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math> is prime to <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mi>q</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">pq</annotation></semantics></math>.

lem:rank-step-trichotomy.label: Lemma 6.36 (The two next-prefix intervals and their gap)
lem:rank-step-trichotomy.note: The Lean statements give the three alternatives for every real target tt (isStraddlePrefix_step_trichotomy); the left endpoint Xu∪{d+1}(2)X_{u\cup\{d+1\}}(2) of the upper interval equals Xu(2)+wd+1X_u(2)+w_{d+1} by positiveMersenneSupportValue_insert, since d+1∉ud+1\notin u. Disjointness is one line from Rd+1<wd+1R_{d+1}<w_{d+1} (mersenneTail_lt_weight) and the strict inequalities defining the gap. For t=1/2t=1/2, IsStraddlePrefix.half_strict makes every endpoint comparison strict and IsStraddlePrefix.half_step_forced gives the three cases as mutually exclusive.

decls.name: Erdos249257.isStraddlePrefix_step_trichotomy
decls.sig:
theorem isStraddlePrefix_step_trichotomy {t : ℝ} {u : Finset ℕ} {d : ℕ}
    (hu : IsStraddlePrefix t u d) :
    IsStraddlePrefix t u (d + 1) ∨
      IsStraddlePrefix t (insert (d + 1) u) (d + 1) ∨
        (positiveMersenneSupportValue (↑u : Set ℕ) + mersenneTail (d + 1) < t ∧
          t < positiveMersenneSupportValue (↑u : Set ℕ)
              + mersenneWeight (d + 1))

decls.name: Erdos249257.IsStraddlePrefix.half_step_forced
decls.sig:
theorem IsStraddlePrefix.half_step_forced {u : Finset ℕ} {d : ℕ}
    (hu : IsStraddlePrefix (1 / 2 : ℝ) u d) :
    (IsStraddlePrefix (1 / 2 : ℝ) u (d + 1) ∧
        ¬ IsStraddlePrefix (1 / 2 : ℝ) (insert (d + 1) u) (d + 1)) ∨
      (IsStraddlePrefix (1 / 2 : ℝ) (insert (d + 1) u) (d + 1) ∧
          ¬ IsStraddlePrefix (1 / 2 : ℝ) u (d + 1)) ∨
        (positiveMersenneSupportValue (↑u : Set ℕ) + mersenneTail (d + 1)
            < 1 / 2 ∧
          (1 / 2 : ℝ) < positiveMersenneSupportValue (↑u : Set ℕ)
            + mersenneWeight (d + 1))

theorem paper_reverse_carry_word :

        (∀ j : ℕ, j < L → a₁ (k + 1 + j) = a₂ (k + 1 + j)) →
        (∀ j : ℕ, j < L → b₁ (k + 1 + j) = b₂ (k + 1 + j)) →
        u₁ (k + L + 1) - u₂ (k + L + 1) = 2 ^ L * (2 * (u₁ k - u₂ k) + 1) ∧
          Odd (2 * (u₁ k - u₂ k) + 1)) ∧
    (∀ (a₁ b₁ u₁ a₂ b₂ u₂ : ℕ → ℤ),

      (∀ m : ℕ, b₂ m + 2 * u₂ m = a₂ m + u₂ (m + 1)) →
      ∀ (k L : ℕ) (B₁ B₂ : ℝ), a₁ k = a₂ k → b₁ k - b₂ k = 1 →
        (∀ j : ℕ, j < L → a₁ (k + 1 + j) = a₂ (k + 1 + j)) →
        (∀ j : ℕ, j < L → b₁ (k + 1 + j) = b₂ (k + 1 + j)) →
        |((u₁ (k + L + 1) : ℤ) : ℝ)| ≤ B₁ →
        |((u₂ (k + L + 1) : ℤ) : ℝ)| ≤ B₂ →
        (2 : ℝ) ^ L ≤ B₁ + B₂) ∧
    (∀ (a₁ b₁ u₁ a₂ b₂ u₂ : ℕ → ℤ),
      (∀ m : ℕ, b₁ m + 2 * u₁ m = a₁ m + u₁ (m + 1)) →
      (∀ m : ℕ, b₂ m + 2 * u₂ m = a₂ m + u₂ (m + 1)) →

        Erdos249257.supportCoeff squarefreeSupport n
          = 2 ^ n.primeFactors.card - 1) ∧

              Erdos249257.supportCoeff squarefreeSupport (N + r) * b ^ (K - r)) ∧
            (∑ r ∈ Finset.Icc (K + 1) L,

            (∃ t : ℕ, 0 < Erdos249257.supportCoeff squarefreeSupport (N + L + 1 + t)) ∧
            q * (C + (N + L + 2)) < b ^ L)) ∧
      (∀ b : ℕ, 2 ≤ b → 2 ∣ b →
        ¬ (∀ q : ℕ, 0 < q → ∃ N K L C : ℕ, K ≤ L ∧
            (∀ r ∈ Finset.Icc 1 K,

            (∑ r ∈ Finset.Icc (K + 1) L,

            (∃ t : ℕ, 0 < Erdos249257.supportCoeff squarefreeSupport (N + L + 1 + t)) ∧

decls.sig:
theorem paper_perturbed_prefixChoice_maximal (F : PerturbedFamily α) {C : ℕ}
    (K : F.AdjacentCut C) [Decidable K.successorCarries]
    (hcap : F.pulseCap < F.gap) :
    K.newCapacity = 4 * C + F.gap ∧
      K.successorCarries = (4 * K.overshoot + K.abovePulse ≤ F.gap) ∧
      K.prefixChoice = (if K.successorCarries then K.above else K.below) ∧
      F.newSum K.prefixChoice ≤ K.newCapacity ∧
      ∀ x : α, F.newSum x ≤ K.newCapacity →
        F.newSum x ≤ F.newSum K.prefixChoice

decls.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR21.paper_perturbed_nextRemainder_three_branches
decls.sig:
theorem paper_perturbed_nextRemainder_three_branches (F : PerturbedFamily α)
    {C : ℕ} (K : F.AdjacentCut C) [Decidable K.successorCarries] :
    K.terminalWeight = 2 * F.gap + 4 ∧
      K.nextRemainder =
        if K.successorCarries then
          F.gap - (4 * K.overshoot + K.abovePulse)
        else if 4 * K.remainder + F.gap - K.belowPulse < K.terminalWeight then
          4 * K.remainder + F.gap - K.belowPulse
        else
          4 * K.remainder - F.gap - K.belowPulse - 4

        u₁ (k + L + 1) - u₂ (k + L + 1) = 2 ^ L * (2 * (u₁ k - u₂ k) + 1) ∧

    (∀ (a₁ b₁ u₁ a₂ b₂ u₂ : ℕ → ℤ),

        |((u₂ (k + L + 1) : ℤ) : ℝ)| ≤ B₂ →

    (∀ (a₁ b₁ u₁ a₂ b₂ u₂ : ℕ → ℤ),

decls.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR21.paper_dynamics
decls.sig:
theorem paper_dynamics {n : ℕ} (hn : 5 ≤ n) {D B D' : Finset ℕ}
    (hD : IsRowLower n D) (hB : IsRowUpper n B) (hD' : IsRowLower (n + 1) D')
    {r o pm pp rem : ℕ}
    (hr : localPrefixQuotient D (2 * n) + r = seamSubsetTarget n)
    (ho : seamSubsetTarget n + o = localPrefixQuotient B (2 * n))
    (hpm : pm = ∑ d ∈ D, rowPulse n d)
    (hpp : pp = ∑ d ∈ B, rowPulse n d)
    (hrem : localPrefixQuotient D' (2 * (n + 1)) + rem = seamSubsetTarget (n + 1)) :
    D = greedySupport n ∧
      pm ≤ 2 * (n - 2) ∧ pp ≤ 2 * (n - 2) ∧
      ((rem : ℤ) =
        if 4 * (o : ℤ) + (pp : ℤ) ≤ 2 ^ (n + 1) then
          (2 : ℤ) ^ (n + 1) - 4 * (o : ℤ) - (pp : ℤ)
        else if 4 * (r : ℤ) + 2 ^ (n + 1) - (pm : ℤ) < 2 ^ (n + 2) + 4 then
          4 * (r : ℤ) + 2 ^ (n + 1) - (pm : ℤ)
        else 4 * (r : ℤ) - 2 ^ (n + 1) - (pm : ℤ) - 4) ∧
      (((rem : ℚ) - 2 ^ (n + 1)) / 2 ^ (n + 1) =
        if 4 * (o : ℤ) + (pp : ℤ) ≤ 2 ^ (n + 1) then
          -((4 * (o : ℚ) + (pp : ℚ)) / 2 ^ (n + 1))
        else if 4 * (r : ℤ) + 2 ^ (n + 1) - (pm : ℤ) < 2 ^ (n + 2) + 4 then
          2 * (((r : ℚ) - 2 ^ n) / 2 ^ n) + 2 - (pm : ℚ) / 2 ^ (n + 1)
        else 2 * (((r : ℚ) - 2 ^ n) / 2 ^ n) - ((pm : ℚ) + 4) / 2 ^ (n + 1))

Under them the Lean statements prove <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>D</mi></msub><mo><</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mi>D</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_D<\Theta_D</annotation></semantics></math>, with <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>D</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mspace width="0.167em"></mspace><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">(</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">)</mo><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi>p</mi><mi>D</mi><mo>−</mo></msubsup><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_D=4\,\mathrm{rem}(D)-p_D^--4</annotation></semantics></math> identified separately, and the bounds <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>≤</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mi>D</mi></msub><mo>≤</mo><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">|</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>D</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">|</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0\le\Theta_D\le|F_D|</annotation></semantics></math>; they add a second conclusion, <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="false"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mstyle><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>D</mi></msub></msub><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">)</mo><mo><</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>D</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tfrac12-X_{D_D}(2)<w_D</annotation></semantics></math>.

    (D : ℕ) (hD13 : 13 ≤ D)
    (hncarry : ¬ (seamAdjacentCut D (by omega)).successorCarries)
    (hmiddle :
      4 * (seamAdjacentCut D (by omega)).remainder +
            (seamPerturbedFamily D (by omega)).gap -
            (seamAdjacentCut D (by omega)).belowPulse <
          (seamAdjacentCut D (by omega)).terminalWeight)
    (hright : ∀ s : ℕ, D + 1 ≤ s →
      seamGreedyWord (s + 1) = (seamGreedyWord s).extend true) :
    (producerCarry
        (insert D
          (↑(seamWordSupport
            (seamAdjacentCut D (by omega)).below) : Set ℕ)) D : ℝ) <
      binaryCoeffTail
        (supportCoeff
          (insert D
            (↑(seamWordSupport

        (2 * D + 2)

thm:nine-way-hub.note: Items (1) to (5) and (7) are each proved equivalent to <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>∈</mo><mi mathvariant="script">𝒜</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1/2\in\mathcal A</annotation></semantics></math>, with branch <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm R</annotation></semantics></math> at row <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math> written as <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>∪</mo><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">{</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{s+1}=D_s\cup\{s\}</annotation></semantics></math> and the omitted ranks in (5) read off the greedy word of row <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_j</annotation></semantics></math>. theorem nextRemainder_trichotomy
    [Decidable K.successorCarries] :
    K.nextRemainder =
      if K.successorCarries then
        F.gap - (4 * K.overshoot + K.abovePulse)
      else if 4 * K.remainder + F.gap - K.belowPulse < K.terminalWeight then
        4 * K.remainder + F.gap - K.belowPulse
      else
        4 * K.remainder - F.gap - K.belowPulse - 4
